title: The incarnate Son remains the Father's own Son by nature
english: The one who alone knows the Father and is known by the Father alone, his wisdom and word, the angel of great counsel, makes the mystery of the plan of salvation with flesh very clear to us. For though he is Son by nature and truly, and though he has shone forth from the very essence of God the Father, he became flesh—that is, a human being—and underwent birth according to the flesh among us, even though he is eternal and always co-existing with the one who begot him. Yet even though he became flesh, the Father knows him as his own Son even in this state. For he said, "The Lord said to me: 'You are my Son; today I have begotten you'" (Psalm 2:7).

title: The Father's twofold begetting of the Son
english: Cyril says: You see the confession at the very start, that is, the declaration. For the Father has set down the words "You are" in order to show the Son's eternal being. He did not become Son in time; he always was this—that is, Son. Then the Father brought in the words "Today I have begotten you" (Psalm 2:7) in order to show his newest birth according to the flesh, which he willingly underwent through the holy Virgin. This is why she has been named Mother of God. For she gave birth not to a mere human being simply joined to God by an external connection, but rather to the very Word from God the Father, who put on human poverty and became a human being like us.

title: Confessing the faith in which we were baptized
english: We have been baptized confessing this faith, and we will not deny the Lord who bought us with his own blood. So when the Father says that he begets today the Son who always exists and is eternal from him—since “today” marks the present moment, that is, the moment of the incarnation—let us understand this: the Father has acknowledged his own Son even when he became flesh, that is, a human being, and he makes his second birth according to the flesh his own as well. For he did not cease to be Son by nature of God the Father because he became a human being. He remained Son even so, and remained in his inherent dignities, even though he was rich and became poor for our sake.
